I validated the submission against the assignment itself, re-ran the code, and opened every cited source. Checklist appended at `playground/cse60745_20261006_e5b94a/validator/checklist.md`.

## What I verified

**Coverage — no gap.** Enumerating the questions myself from the ingest pages (not from `problems.json`): Q1 GCN, Q2 GAT, Q3 GIN, Q4 R-GCN, Q5 deep — 5 × 6 = 30 pts, all answered in order, cover page present. The one embedded figure (`page_002_fig_01.png`, read at native resolution) is the `MyGCNConv` stub and pins the four required method signatures; all five classes implement all four.

**Correctness — I re-ran it.** I pulled all five `lstlisting` blocks out of the *final* `.tex` files (so I tested the code a grader reads, not the worker's `layers.py`) and ran them against PyG with weights copied across:

| layer | reference | max abs diff |
|---|---|---|
| `MyGCNConv` | `GCNConv` | 0.0 |
| `MyGATConv` | `GATConv` | 0.0 |
| `MyGINConv` | `GINConv` | 0.0 |
| `MyRGCNConv` | `RGCNConv(aggr='mean')` | 4.8e-07 |
| `MyDeepConv` | `APPNP(K=8, α=0.3)` | 0.0 |

Every number in Table 1 traces to `results.json`; I recomputed the Q5 seed means (the 45% drop, the flat 0.725s), re-ran `gin_probe.py` to confirm Q3's 0.87/0.63/22.9×/2.1×, and checked Q4's chance baseline by hand (H₂₁/21 = 0.174). Parameter counts reproduce. Notably, the master's one edit to the worker's prose — 0.726 → 0.725 at 4 hops — is the *correct* value (true mean 0.72549), and it added two captions the worker had omitted.

**R9 — I opened all three papers.** Both APPNP quotes are verbatim and the paper's next paragraph is exactly the fix attributed to it; "proportional to the square root of the vertex degree" is Li et al.'s own wording, and their Conclusions defer deep-compatible filters to future work, so "does not make deep propagation safe" is accurate rather than a straw man; Schlichtkrull's Eq. (2) and link-prediction normalisation are both characterised correctly.

**The PDF.** Rebuilt from source: clean exit, 8 pages, **zero overfull hboxes**. Figure legible at printed size and showing what the text claims. Lint passes.

## Why this is a FAIL

One major defect, three minor:

- **[D1.1, major]** Q4's prose is ~340 words against a ~228-word R8 target for a single-part 6-point question — ~50% over, past the quarter threshold, with no sub-part justifying it. The excess is the closing paragraph's normalisation ablation (`The normalisation is the lever:` → end, 54 words, plus the ± spread clause) — an experiment the question did not ask for. The "the layer is not the cause" verification *is* load-bearing and should stay. Cut ~80–110 words.
- **[D1.2, minor]** Schlichtkrull et al. is leaned on three times in Q4, including "their Eq. (2)", but has no bibliography entry — the References list only Li and Gasteiger. Master-level fix, since the bibliography lives in `p1b.tex`.
- **[D1.3, minor]** The document opens with an unheaded "All four layers were run..." paragraph above Q1 — true of p1's four layers, confusing as the first line of a five-question submission where Q4 uses a different harness.
- **[D1.4, minor]** The gensim non-determinism caveat appears in both Q4 and Q5 (different feature matrices, so neither is wrong, but it reads as repeated boilerplate).

I explicitly did **not** flag Q5's length (407 words): it genuinely demands four things and lands 17% over the scaled multi-sub-part ceiling, under the threshold. I also withdrew an α-selection concern — α=0.3 did win the earlier (α, dropout) grid.

VERDICT: FAIL
